scope: Five additions approved after comparing the supplied conservation and funding list with the 27 existing grants. This is an additive supplement, not a replacement or full re-verification of the 19 October survey.
verificationNotes: Upcoming rounds remain discoverable but are not labelled open or included in closing soon. No invented opening or closing dates are stored as deadlines.

The FRRR program heading and funding calendar agree on 3 December 2026; the calendar specifies 5 pm. Lower program copy also mentions rolling applications, so the listing asks readers to confirm the current window.

Lismore and Byron direct page requests were blocked. Official indexed content was checked, with its limits recorded per entry. Byron indexed material retains 2025/26 figures: no unsupported 2026 amount or deadline is imported.
Big Scrub Rainforest Conservancy and Byron's habitat restoration register are support pathways in conservation-support.json, not duplicate cash grants.
Property-specific information from the supplied notes is excluded from all public listings.

entries.title: FRRR — Strengthening Rural Communities: Capacity Building
entries.summary: Training and specialist support to strengthen rural not-for-profits and their communities' social resilience to drought.
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible not-for-profits serving agriculture-dependent rural and regional communities, with an ABN or incorporation certificate, or an approved legal organisation supporting the application.
entries.eligibilitySummary: For rural not-for-profits building organisational capacity and social resilience to drought; individual and commercial applications are ineligible.
entries.notes: The published application window closes at 5 pm on 3 December 2026, NSW time. Projects must build capacity and demonstrate community benefit and drought preparedness. Eligible activities include specialist advice, training and mentoring. Website or app creation, subscriptions and equipment purchases are excluded. Confirm the current window with FRRR because the page also describes rolling applications subject to available funds.
entries.verificationMethod: Official program page and funding calendar
entries.verificationNote: FRRR lists a 3 December deadline and also mentions rolling applications. Confirm the current application window directly.

entries.title: Lismore City Council — Rural Landholders Initiative
entries.summary: Support for biodiversity restoration on rural land in Lismore LGA. Council's annual EOI window starts in November; exact next-round dates and applicant stream are to be confirmed.
entries.funding: Published program amounts: up to $15,000 for individual landholders and $50,000 for community groups; confirm the next round's stream and conditions
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible rural landholders with properties larger than 2 hectares in Lismore LGA, and eligible community groups under the applicable stream. Projects must protect or improve biodiversity, include cash or in-kind contributions and ongoing maintenance, and meet Council's rates requirements.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Lismore LGA rural biodiversity projects; contributions and ongoing maintenance required. Confirm whether the next round accepts individual or group applications.
entries.notes: Not confirmed open. Council publishes November EOIs and a 1 July start for successful projects the following year, without exact next-round dates on the checked page. Ask the Rural Landholder Initiative Officer which applicant stream is offered and obtain current guidelines before preparing an application.
entries.verificationMethod: Official council indexed page; direct access blocked
entries.verificationNote: Exact next-round dates and applicant stream have not been confirmed.

entries.title: Byron Shire Council — Regenerative Agriculture Small Grants
entries.summary: Support for Byron Shire farmers improving soil health, biodiversity and farm productivity through regenerative land management. Retained to track future rounds.
entries.funding: Confirm the next round's grant amount with Council
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible primary producers, market gardeners and small-scale farmers in Byron Shire, subject to the current round's land and applicant requirements.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Byron Shire farming projects; check the next round's eligibility and funding cap.
entries.notes: Closed-round reference. Council's indexed program and grants pages say applications are closed, but retain older dates and funding figures. No new opening date, funding cap or current application deadline was independently confirmed. Contact Council's Agricultural Extension Officer or check the program page for the next round.
entries.verificationMethod: Official council indexed pages; direct access blocked
entries.verificationNote: Council's indexed pages retain older round details. Confirm any new dates and funding amounts directly.

entries.title: Rous County Council — Community Grants
entries.summary: Community activities and events aligned with Rous's services and public benefit. Council announces the next application round opens on 1 June 2027.
entries.funding: $1,000–$2,500 excluding GST under the published program; confirm 2027 conditions when applications open
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible organisations, incorporated not-for-profits, businesses, schools, universities, sports clubs and associations in Ballina, Byron, Kyogle, Lismore, Richmond Valley or Tweed LGAs. Public liability insurance is required.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Eligible organisations across six Northern Rivers LGAs; activities must align with Rous's services and deliver public benefit.
entries.notes: The 2026 round is closed. Council confirms the 2027 round opens on 1 June 2027. No exact 2027 closing date is recorded here. Check updated guidelines and the application form when the round opens; the page still includes past 2026 application dates.

entries.title: NSW Biodiversity Conservation Trust — Rainforest Conservation Offer
entries.summary: A competitive conservation offer providing annual management payments to successful landholders who permanently protect qualifying rainforest. Expressions of interest are closed.
entries.funding: Annual payments based on the agreed conservation area and management plan; no standard grant amount
entries.whoCanApply: Eligible landowners within the mapped offer area in Ballina, Byron, Kyogle, Lismore, Richmond Valley and Tweed LGAs, willing to enter an in-perpetuity agreement. Published site requirements include at least 20 hectares of native vegetation, including 15 hectares of qualifying rainforest in moderate to good condition.
entries.eligibilitySummary: Mapped North Coast offer area, qualifying rainforest and a permanent agreement; this offer has its own minimum-area requirements.
entries.notes: EOIs closed on 29 June 2026. Later assessment and agreement dates relate to existing applicants, not a new application window. No reopening has been announced. This payment-based offer is separate from Conservation Partners Grants; smaller-site exceptions for other BCT agreements should not be assumed to apply.
entries.verificationMethod: Official BCT offer page and published offer timeline
